extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Human Relations journal (SAGE/Tavistock Institute) / invited academic referees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers conducting double‑blind peer review for the Human Relations journal, covering ethics, how to view and score manuscripts, composing confidential and author-facing comments, file attachments, symbol use, and submission mechanics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected publication/duplication/ethics/conflict problems
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers suspect any of the following problems with any article that they are reviewing, we recommend that they contact the journal editor to discuss the situation without delay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspicions include: the paper has been either published or submitted to another journal; the paper is duplicating the work of others; there might be problems with the ethics of the research conducted; there might be an undeclared conflict of interest attached to the paper. Keep all information about such matters confidential and do not discuss them with colleagues other than the journal editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and disclose conflicts of interest before reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Think carefully about their own potential conflicts of interest relating to the paper before undertaking the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the editor if you become aware of the identity of the author during blind peer review. Be careful about potential conflicts and consult the editor if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid biased judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful not to make judgements about the paper based on personal, financial, intellectual biases or any other considerations than the quality of the research and written presentation of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate only on research quality and presentation; do not allow unrelated personal or financial factors to influence your assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pass invitation or involve others without editor permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should not pass on the invitation or involve anyone else in the review process without first consulting the handling editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need assistance or wish to invite a colleague, get explicit permission from the handling editor first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing the manuscript
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways for you to view the manuscript assigned to you: download to a printer or read directly from your screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you wish to view the manuscript and the review form simultaneously, click on the manuscript title; it will open in a new window. Leave the new window open, switch back to the main window, and open the score sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Conceptual contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual contribution: let the editor know how the manuscript rates in terms of its conceptual contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The score sheet should be completed in all fields. In addition to qualitative comments, indicate your ratings on conceptual contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Methodological contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological contribution: let the editor know how the manuscript rates in terms of its methodological contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete this field on the score sheet to indicate the manuscript's methodological contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Overall contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall contribution: let the editor know how the manuscript rates in terms of its overall contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an assessment of the manuscript's overall contribution on the score sheet in addition to detailed comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Appropriateness of methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of methods: let the editor know how appropriate the methods are for the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether chosen methods are suitable and justify your rating in the comments; complete the corresponding score sheet field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Methodological rigour
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological rigour: rate how rigorous the methods and execution are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comment specifically on methodological rigour and fill in the score sheet field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Integration of theoretical framework and data
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration of theoretical framework and data: rate how well theory and data are integrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report on how effectively the theoretical framework is linked to the empirical evidence; complete the score sheet field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score sheet completion — Practical relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical relevance: let the editor know how practically relevant the manuscript is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate and comment on the practical relevance (implications) of the work in the score sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments to Editor — contextual information only
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual information only: use this section for confidential comments to the editor ONLY for contextual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include such things as how confident you are in your ability to assess the paper. All substantive comment on the paper itself must appear in the Comments to Author section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments to Author — substantive comments and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: These comments WILL be conveyed to the author and any other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space to convey to the Author and Editor your comments on the paper, suggested changes, etc. Please number your review comments to make it easier for the editor to refer to specific comments in the decision letter. Please DO NOT include decision recommendations in this section; instead, select one of the decision options in the Recommendation section. Please comment specifically on the use of analytic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid attachments; paste comments into the field
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid attaching files – please ONLY use the file attachment option for graphical representations, such as suggested changes to tables or figures; please paste your Comments to the Author(s) into the appropriate field instead of attaching them as a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need to attach a file because your review comments contain a table or figure, you may attach a file provided: (1) you have removed document properties and personal information to maintain anonymity; (2) you have completed the score sheet itself; (3) you have clicked on the 'This file is for the Author and Editor' radial button and clicked 'Attach' after selecting files. Do not attach PDF files (they require anonymization). Reviewers can review author-provided supplements via their Reviewer Centre by clicking 'Files' on the Review Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: File anonymization requirements for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: To maintain your anonymity and double-blind peer review, you have removed the 'Document properties and personal information' (in MS Word, see under File on the menu bar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attach PDF files, as these require anonymization of the file creator before they can be forwarded to the author(s) and any reviewers. Ensure you click the correct radial button and 'Attach' when uploading files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain-text symbols and spell out special characters
rubrics_metrics.description: As with other plain text transmissions, such as e-mail, your use of special symbols is restricted. Please use symbols that are found on your keyboard and plain text notations, such as (^) for superscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out Greek letters (e.g. µ -> mu). If you will be repeatedly using a Greek letter, you can re-define the symbol (e.g. G = gamma) at the beginning of the section in which you will be using it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save as Draft then Submit to finalize review
rubrics_metrics.description: It is essential that you first click the 'Save as Draft' button located beneath the review, otherwise, none of the information that you have entered will be saved in the system!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may also save the review as a file on your own computer using cut-and-paste. You MUST click on the 'Submit' button to finalize your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow COPE and SAGE reviewer resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Full guidelines for peer reviewers can be found on the COPE website and detailed guidance is available via the SAGE Reviewer Gateway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the SAGE Reviewer Gateway topics (Ethics & Responsibility, How to Review an Article, Online Submission & Peer Review System, Purpose of Peer Review, Resources & FAQs, Reviewer Rewards) and apply COPE ethical guidance when in doubt.
